subject: Discovery recap & procurement framing — Brightline Health
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & procurement framing — Brightline Health

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and a clear procurement path: 

Pain points you shared
- High latency on current in-house inference for triage (p95 often > 800ms), causing clinician friction.
- Cost volatility with current third-party APIs during spikes.
- Strict PHI handling requirements and auditability for models that touch patient data.

Current stack and constraints
- Primary NLP currently routed to internal on-prem LLMs (fine-tuned) with fallback to 3rd-party API for burst traffic.
- SSO via Okta, centralized logging, and existing SOC 2 Type II report.

Success criteria for a pilot / eval
1) End-to-end response p95 < 200ms for triage queries under target load (burst-friendly).
2) Reproducible privacy controls: tenant isolation, KMS-managed keys, and audit log exports.
3) Unit economics: predictable per-token cost at scale (target: < $X per 1M tokens; we included guardrail scenarios in the attached pricing doc).

Procurement/decision process you described
- Timeline: internal decision window ~targeted for mid-July (you noted July 15 as the approximate decision date).
- Stakeholders to involve: Product (you), Procurement (Karen Liu), Security/Legal for SOC2/contracting.
- Two commercial paths: hosted metered pilot (low friction) or dedicated reserved capacity (SLA-backed, commit).

Attachments: I attached a short pricing guardrails PDF and a technical POC checklist to help scope the POC and procurement ask.

Proposed next steps
1) Confirm stakeholders and procurement timeline (can you confirm Karen's procurement email and whether legal needs an NDA or any specific contract language?).
2) Redwood proposes a 4-week technical POC scoped to demo: latency targets, privacy controls, and a simple cost run-rate.
3) I’ll connect Marissa (commercial lead) and Vivek (solutions lead) into a single procurement sync once you confirm stakeholders — we can bring initial commercial guardrails and an MSA/term outline.

If that matches your view, I’ll send a calendar invite for a procurement + tech sync next week and include the draft guardrails for review.

Thanks again — short on details here to keep the thread concise, happy to expand on any point.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood-pricing-guardrails.pdf, technical-POC-checklist.xlsx

Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap — that aligns with what I heard internally. Couple quick clarifications and notes from my side:

- Stakeholders: I’m looping Karen (Procurement) on this thread; she’ll own contracting/PO. Security/Legal will want to review SOC2 and data handling specifics (they generally want to see a scope statement).
- Timeline: July 15 decision target is correct; we’d like a POC to start by mid-June if possible and run ~4 weeks.
- Price ask: Can you provide two ballpark commercial guardrails — a pilot-metered option (no commit) and a 3-month reserved option with an estimate? We need rough numbers to justify the POC to finance.
- NDA: We have a standing one for some vendors, but I’ll confirm and loop legal if needed.

I’ve quoted your original message below for context. Once you share the ballpark numbers, I’ll coordinate a procurement sync with Karen.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product, Clinical AI | Brightline Health
alyssa@brightlinehealth.com | (617) 555-3388

Alyssa / Karen —

Appreciate the quick reply and confirmation of timeline. To make the procurement sync productive, here are two initial commercial guardrails (high level) we can use for internal justification — final numbers will depend on exact throughput and token mix, but these should be directionally useful: 

Option A — Hosted pilot (metered)
- No commit pilot for 4 weeks.
- Estimated run-rate: $2,500–$6,000 for the POC depending on throughput and model selection.
- Pros: minimal contracting friction, fast start.
- Cons: no SLA-backed latency guarantee; suitable for validation only.

Option B — Dedicated reserved (short-term)
- 3-month reserved capacity with an ingress commit (monthly billing).
- Estimated starting monthly cost: $28k–$45k (depends on GPU class and expected concurrent request volume).
- Pros: SLA, predictable latency and cost, priority capacity during spikes.
- Cons: short-term commit required.

Commercial extras: we can provide a short-term credit for the pilot if Brightline moves to a reserved path within 60 days. We will also include SOC2 evidence, SSO flow docs, and a short scope statement for legal review (attached in the procurement playbook).

Next steps (proposed)
1) I’ll create a shared drive doc with the MAP / mutual action plan and populate contacts, timeline, and what we’ll deliver in the POC: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/BRIGHT-2247
2) Proposed procurement + tech sync: Fri Jun 18 or Mon Jun 21 — I’ll send invites; please let me know preferred times.
3) I’ll drop a draft MSA/term summary and a simple DocuSign link for the pilot MSA so legal can review ahead of the vendor meeting: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/MSA-BRIGHT-2247

Marissa (commercial) and Vivek (solutions) — looping you in to own the commercial estimate and POC success criteria respectively.

Happy to jump on a quick call this afternoon if that helps finalize the sync time.

Best,
